Hi Marissa,

Thanks for taking this on. Attached is our RFP worksheet and the dedicated capacity questionnaire — we need detailed answers around GPU types, sustained throughput (tokens/sec), peak concurrency, burst behavior, and reservation/commitment options for a 12–24 month contract. A few specifics:

- Baseline inference workload: ~2.5M tokens/day (averaged) across 3 geographies, but traffic is spiky with day-of-week peaks.
- Expected peak concurrent sessions: 120-160 for short-chat workflows (avg 60-120 tokens per call), and up to 10 long-form synth tasks (avg 1,200 tokens) during overnight windows.
- Latency target for chat: p95 < 300ms for responses up to 256 tokens; for long-form jobs p95 < 1.5s.
- Security: need VPC/private deployment for production, but initial pilot can be hosted.

Can you return the completed questionnaire and a short slide or PDF that maps required GPUs and expected throughput for both pilot and production scenarios? We have a procurement review on 2026-05-07.

Thanks,

Appreciate the detail. Attaching our completed questionnaire and a preliminary sizing PDF that covers two scenarios: Pilot (hosted, 3-month) and Prod (VPC/dedicated, 12–24 month commit). High level notes up front:

- Pilot recommendation: 4x A10G (or equivalent) with autoscale to 8 for burst windows; expected sustained throughput ~18k tokens/sec across the pool, p95 chat latency ~180-250ms for 256-token responses.
- Production recommendation: reserved pool of 12x A100-80G (or 24x H100-80G quantized profiles depending on model selection) to meet 160 concurrent chat sessions and 10 long-form jobs with headroom. Sustained throughput ~80k tokens/sec; with caching/batching we project >30% cost reduction vs naive provisioning.
- Reservation planning: monthly commitments with a 10–15% burst buffer; we can structure a 12-month reserved capacity contract with quarterly scale review.

Rajiv / Marissa —

Quick technical addendum to the PDF: below are the assumptions and a sizing table excerpt.

Assumptions:
- Chat model: 13B decoder (quantized 4-bit fastpath) for most chat; long-form synth uses a 70B LM variant (quantized 8-bit or mixed) for higher quality.
- Avg tokens per chat RPC: 90 tokens generated (60-120 range); avg tokens/sec per GPU based on bench: A100-80G (fp16) ~12k tokens/sec for 13B; H100-80G ~18k tokens/sec.
- Batching and prefix KV cache assumed for conversational sessions; effective per-GPU throughput improvements accounted for.

Sizing table (summary):
- Pilot (hosted): 4x A10G (baseline) -> 4 GPUs * 4.5k tok/s (13B quantized) = ~18k tok/s; headroom for 8x during bursts.
- Prod conservative: 12x A100-80G -> 12 * 12k = 144k tok/s theoretical; practical sustained ~80k tok/s with mixed workloads and KV overhead. This comfortably covers 160 concurrent chat sessions + 10 long jobs with p95 targets.
- Prod aggressive: 24x H100-80G quantized mixed (preferred for latency-sensitive setups) -> sustained ~200k tok/s, lower tail latency and better headroom for spikes.

Reservation planning notes:
- Commitment tiers: 12 GPU-months, 36 GPU-months, 120 GPU-months (we price per-GPU-hour with step discounts at each tier).
- Autoscale: we recommend a baseline reserved pool + burst cluster that can use preemptible capacity for non-critical long-form jobs to reduce cost.

Open question for procurement/architecture: do you have any mandatory GPU vendor requirements (e.g., H100 only) or is a performance/cost trade-off acceptable? If H100 is required, we’ll prepare the alternate pricing.

Ben Carter

Thanks for the questions. Summary answers below — I’ve attached an updated pricing summary and a short p95 latency table for inclusion in your packet. Full technical appendix and the HSM/audit export checklist are attached as well.

1) p95 latency envelope (included as a small table in attached PDF):
- A100-80G (13B quantized): 256-token response p95 ~220ms; 1,200-token job p95 ~1.1s.
- H100-80G (13B quantized): 256-token response p95 ~150-180ms; 1,200-token job p95 ~0.8-0.95s.

2) Ramp & pricing: we propose a staged commitment credit: sign 12-month at Tier-1 pricing; if you scale committed GPUs by >=50% within the first 6 months, we retrospectively apply a Tier-2 discount to the initial months (credit applied at month 7). We can formalize a table in the term sheet.

3) Security: dedicated VPC supports KMS/HSM integrations (we support AWS KMS, CloudHSM and customer-managed HSM via key wrapping). Audit logs (per-request metadata, latency, tokens consumed) can be exported to S3 or directly streamed to Splunk/Datadog/your SIEM on a 1m/5m cadence.
